headline: PAGASA Tracks Two LPAs as Habagat Keeps Red Warnings Across Central Luzon
seoTitle: PAGASA Tracks 2 LPAs, Habagat Rain Risk | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA monitored two low-pressure areas on August 28 as Habagat rains kept Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and parts of Bulacan and Tarlac under Red warnings.
deck: One LPA was inside PAR east-northeast of Itbayat and another was farther east outside PAR, while serious flooding remained possible in Red-warning areas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA was monitoring two low-pressure areas on Friday afternoon, August 28, as the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat continued to bring heavy rain over parts of Luzon.

As of 2 p.m., the newly formed LPA outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility was about 1,460 kilometers east of Central Luzon. The LPA inside PAR was later estimated at 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes.

sections.heading: Development potential
paragraphs: PAGASA assessed both disturbances as having a medium chance of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours. Their future tracks and any eventual local cyclone names remained dependent on further development and position.

The agency's 4 p.m. public forecast identified the LPA inside PAR and the Habagat as the weather systems affecting the country; it did not establish that either disturbance had already become a tropical cyclone.

sections.heading: Habagat remains a concern
paragraphs: At 11 p.m., Red rainfall warnings remained in force over Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and specified areas of Bulacan and Tarlac, where serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas. Orange and Yellow warnings covered other specified areas in Central and Southern Luzon.
PAGASA's broader outlook also warned that accumulated rainfall and saturated ground could worsen flooding and landslide impacts even when rain temporarily weakens.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Rainfall-warning colors and LPA positions can change within hours. This report distinguishes the short-fuse regional warnings from broader rainfall outlooks and does not treat forecast tracks as fixed.

Malacañang suspended government work and classes at all levels in Metro Manila and 16 provinces beginning at 1 p.m. Friday because of the Habagat and the possibility of further enhancement by the LPA inside PAR.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings, local disaster advisories and any subsequent tropical cyclone bulletins if either LPA develops further.
